stories.title: Senate blocks move to withdraw diplomatic passport privileges from state ministers, advisers
summary: According to the copy of the bill available with Dawn, it sought to amend the Passports Act 1974 by inserting a new Section 12A for restriction on diplomatic passport entitlement of ministers of state, advisers, special assistants, federal secretaries and director generals.
The bill, moved by PPP’s Senator Rehman, sought to amend the Islamabad Capital Territory (Prohibition of Plastic Book Covers) Act 2026.

It called upon the government of Pakistan to continue extending political, moral and diplomatic support to the people of IoK and to intensify its efforts to highlight the Kashmir dispute at the international level.

stories.title: Actor Walter Koenig, Star Trek's Pavel Chekov, dies at 90
summary: Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series Star Trek and seven subsequent feature films, has died at the age of 90. “My heart is heavy.
Star Trek creator Gene Roddenberry picked Koenig, who had played only a few prior roles on television, when he decided to add a Russian character to the crew of the fictional Starship Enterprise.

They were often typecast because they were so closely associated with Star Trek. “Most of the ‘70s, I didn’t work at all, and I blamed ⁠it on typecasting,” Koenig told the St. Petersburg Times in 1998.

stories.title: Pezeshkian urges 'regional unity' in meeting with Makkah pact countries in Tehran
summary: Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster earlier shared a video of the meeting, saying the quadrilateral meeting on “regional security and stability” had begun.

At the start of the meeting, Iran’s state broadcaster reported the meeting was bringing together Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to discuss “regional cooperation, the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its consequences”, among other topics.
According to Iran’s ISNA news agency, Baqaei said during the media briefing that the suggestion for the meeting was made during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran last week.

stories.title: Govt orders review of existing drug pricing formula to ensure medicines are priced fairly
summary: Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Cheema, who chaired a meeting of the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap), directed officials to expedite the processing of pending drug-pricing cases after being briefed that their case-by-case evaluation was almost complete.
Officials told the meeting that Drap was reviewing the existing drug-pricing formula and examining provisions that could hinder the determination of fair and accurate prices.
Cheema ordered that the pricing mechanism should remain people-centred while avoiding unnecessary barriers for importers and pharmaceutical companies.

stories.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence.
It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year.
Around 27pc of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer.

stories.title: UN raises 'ethnic cleansing' concerns over Israel's operation in West Bank's Hebron
summary: Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank’s Hebron city, launched after a deadly attack by Palestinian gunmen, raises serious concerns of “ethnic cleansing”, the United Nations (UN) warned Monday.
The municipality in Hebron, the Palestinian territory’s largest city, said in a statement that 3,189 people had been forced from their homes by the ongoing operation.
It followed Friday’s attack in which two Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers at a checkpoint near the city, just days before Tuesday’s Israeli elections.

stories.title: Rs11tr tax exemptions granted in five years
summary: The National Assembly was informed on Monday that tax exemptions worth Rs11.047 trillion were granted over the last five years, while the government was preparing a new policy to provide relief to low-income households facing high liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices.

Responding to a Calling Attention Notice on rising LPG prices, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had held two to three meetings to address the LPG price issue.
The minister said the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority's (OGRA) notified rate of Rs280 applied to locally produced LPG, while no policy was currently in place for imported supplies.

stories.title: Swift sale of USC assets ordered
summary: In response, the Finance Division advised USC to expedite the realisation of proceeds from the disposal of properties and assets, and submit a case for approval of a technical supplementary grant of Rs11.98 billion.
The ECC was requested to approve Rs11.329 billion as a technical supplementary grant for USC to meet its immediate financing requirements and facilitate completion of the closure process.

The ECC had approved a supplementary grant of Rs30.216 billion to pay off the employees' severance package and other dues, clear the outstanding liabilities of suppliers and meet expenditures pertaining to the continuation of operations till the eventual privatisation of USC.

stories.title: Banking links sought with Ethiopia
summary: The minister briefed him on reforms under way in Pakistan aimed at lasting economic stability and investment-led growth, and both sides discussed sharing development experience given similarities in their economic structures.
The two sides also discussed air connectivity between Pakistan and Ethiopia and its role in strengthening commercial and people-to-people links.

The minister reaffirmed Pakistan's interest in strengthening economic relations with Ethiopia, and both sides expressed commitment to continued engagement on trade, investment, financial cooperation and connectivity.

stories.title: PSX recovers from policy rate-driven sell-off
summary: Bulls returned to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Monday as buying re-emerged in index-heavy sectors in the latter half of trading, reversing the early fall amid anxiety ahead of the State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) policy rate decision.

Trading remained volatile amid earlier concerns over a potential 100-basis-point rate hike, while buying interest emerged later, particularly in cement, which helped the index recover to close in positive territory.

"The market traded in both directions amid cautious investor sentiment ahead of the SBP's MPC announcement, with market participants largely anticipating a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib commented.

stories.title: CDWP approves 10 projects worth Rs40.9b
summary: The third referral is the Prime Minister's Solar Scheme for Newly Merged Districts, valued at Rs13,323 million, approved in principle to provide off-grid solar energy solutions to households.

The party also approved in principle revamping Pakistan Television Corporation (PTVC) at Rs3,962.250 million and a pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at the 220kV Jhimpir-I grid station at Rs4,394.720 million.

It approved an eight-lane overhead bridge at Imamia Colony Railway Crossing, Shahdara, at Rs7,492.050 million, and recommended widening of National Highway N-45 from Chakdara to Timergara, 39 kilometres, at Rs17,012.323 million to ECNEC, to be financed through Exim Bank.

stories.title: Uncertainty subsides over rise in reserves, tax receipts
summary: The decline indicates that businesses and investors saw a more stable policy environment during the month, although concerns over fuel prices, subsidies and delayed talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) continued to weigh on sentiment.
The Lahore School Trade Policy Uncertainty Index declined 22.1% month-on-month to 192.89 in September.
The Lahore School Investment Policy Uncertainty Index fell 6.45% month-on-month to 145, supported by progress on power-sector reforms and Pakistan's successful return to international debt markets.

stories.title: Govt to maintain wheat reserves of up to 6m tonnes to ensure uninterrupted supply: minister
summary: The minister said that the federal government, under the leadership of PM Shehbaz, was taking comprehensive measures to strengthen agricultural productivity, improve market regulation and ensure the availability of essential food commodities across the country.

Endorsing the government’s pledge to export wheat next year, Pakistan Kissan Ittehad President Khalid Mahmood Khokhar appreciated the government’s decision to fix the indicative wheat price at Rs4500 per 40kg.

Last month, the Pakistan Kissan Ittehad demanded a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price for wheat, warning that farmers may not sow wheat for the next season if the government delays announcing crop policies.

stories.title: Central Development Working Party refers 3 KP infrastructure projects worth Rs100bn to Ecnec
summary: The CDWP meeting also cleared another 11 projects throughout the country with an estimated investment of nearly Rs126.50bn, including a mega project worth Rs85.34bn in Punjab.
Of them, Rs40.9bn worth of 10 smaller projects were approved by the CDWP, while four other larger projects were recommended to Ecnec for formal approval.

The PM’s Youth Development Centres project, valued at Rs4.15bn was approved in principle, incorporating third-party validation and structured monitoring frameworks to ensure effective resource utilisation.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks investment from US in oil refinery upgradation projects
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Monday sought investment from US financial institutions in its oil refinery upgradation projects as the two countries discussed increasing cooperation in the energy sector.
During the meeting, Malik briefed the US envoy on measures Pakistan was taking to ensure energy security amid the evolving geopolitical situation, an official statement said.

She emphasised the importance of creating opportunities for US companies in Pakistan and expressed optimism about establishing long-term energy supply contracts, noting that such arrangements would be mutually beneficial and create opportunities for American businesses, it said.

stories.title: Former army chief Abdul Waheed Kakar passes away in Rawalpindi
summary: Former army chief retired General Abdul Waheed Kakar passed away in Rawalpindi on Monday, a statement by the military’s media affairs wing said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, expressing condolences at the death of the former general, paid tribute to his “invaluable services” to the Pakistan Armed Forces, state broadcaster PTV reported.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in a post on X, said he was “deeply saddened” by Kakar’s passing. “His distinguished service to Pakistan and the Pakistan Army will be remembered with the highest regard,” Dar wrote, praying for the deceased’s family.

stories.title: Lucky Group, Qatar Energy consortium quits Port Qasim LNG terminal plan over 'policy changes'
summary: The Energas chairman contended that those issues remain unresolved to date, which could have led to a final investment decision (FID) by Qatar Energy and Pakistani partners. “The government had committed to resolving these matters following discussions with the State of Qatar.

He added that the national energy requirements and the policy environment had materially evolved since the project was originally conceived and Energas had already approached PQA for the return/refund of the partial concession fee.
Energas said Pakistan’s official Integrated Energy Study (IES) — Final Report of March 28, 2025 confirmed that no new LNG terminals were required over the next five years.

stories.title: From protests to power: How Serbia's students triumphed
summary: Serbia’s long-running student protest movement celebrated a historic win in the country’s election, ending 14 years of rule by the country’s right-wing populist leader Aleksandar Vucic.
Here some key points about Serbia’s student-led movement as its candidates prepare to form government.
The movement has not said who would be prime minister, leaving open who will lead the government, Vucicevic said.

stories.title: Remembering former army chief Gen Abdul Waheed Kakar
summary: Former army chief retired Gen Abdul Waheed Kakar, who played a decisive role in resolving Pakistan’s 1993 political crisis, passed away in Rawalpindi on Monday at the age of 89.

Gen Kakar is best remembered for helping end a serious confrontation between then-president Ghulam Ishaq Khan and then-prime minister Nawaz Sharif in 1993, when the country seemed on the brink of another prolonged political crisis and the government stood paralysed.
Gen Kakar received several military honours during his career, including the Nishan-i-Imtiaz (Military) and the Hilal-i-Imtiaz (Military).

stories.title: Khawaja Asif hints at 'progress' in Makkah alliance’s talks with Iran on Saudi-Houthi conflict
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Monday hinted at the possibility of "progress" in a meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance members with Iran, stating that the participants had likely arrived at a "conclusion" to end Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Houthis.
Members of the Makkah Defence Alliance and Iran agreed to continue further dialogue in an effort to ramp up cooperation for regional peace and security after a high-level meeting in Tehran.
Asif further noted that Saudi Arabia's war with Yemen started in March 2014, and it had been Pakistan’s commitment ever since to defend the kingdom.

stories.title: Imaan, Hadi move SC against IHC order refusing to stay trial in security breach case
summary: The plea argued that the trial court proceeded with unprecedented haste by recording the examination-in-chief of six prosecution witnesses on Oct 10 and 14, and accepting the prosecution’s request to shift the trial to jail.
The decision to conduct the trial in jail had also been challenged before the IHC, with the petition pointing out that the trial court had appointed state counsel.
During the proceedings, Advocate Azad noted that the decision to conduct the trial inside the jail had been challenged before the IHC.

stories.title: Pope fit enough to make Latin America trip next month, Vatican says
summary: Pope Leo's trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru will go ahead, the Vatican said on Monday, indicating that Leo's recovery from lung cancer surgery was on track and that he was fit enough to make the November 6-17 ​journey.

"The Holy Father’s recovery after the surgery continues, and the latest medical examinations ​attest to his good health and favorable clinical condition," the Vatican said in a statement, citing Leo's ​personal physician Luigi Carbone.

Leo had spent decades as a missionary in Peru before his predecessor Francis called him back to Rome in 2023 and promoted him to Vatican positions, so the trip will mark a homecoming ​of sorts for the ​first US pontiff.

stories.title: Govt hikes petrol by Rs1.54, diesel by Rs2.16 for Oct 27
summary: The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.54 and Rs2.16 per litre, respectively, for October 27.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

Oil prices inched higher after falling more than $2 a ‌barrel on Monday, as persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary and prices near six-month highs, even as diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict in the Middle East resumed.

stories.title: Where have Karachi’s Olive Ridley turtles gone?
summary: Once familiar visitors to Pakistan’s sandy shores, Olive Ridley sea turtles have all but vanished from the country’s recorded nesting grounds.
Now, the discovery of a dead turtle on Clifton Beach has brought an old ecological mystery into focus: if these turtles still inhabit the Arabian Sea, where have the breeding females gone?

Olive Ridleys continue to inhabit the Arabian Sea, leaving scientists with a crucial unanswered question: have Pakistan’s breeding females shifted to distant shores, or are other factors disrupting their nesting cycle?

stories.title: Bride shot dead after her walima reception, allegedly by jilted suitor in Gujranwala
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2039797/bride-shot-dead-after-her-walima-reception-by-jilted-suitor-in-gujranwala

stories.title: Central bank raises policy rate by 50 basis points to 12pc
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday raised the key policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 per cent, its first increase since April as inflation, fuelled by high energy costs due to the Gulf conflict, remained above target.

The inflation outlook is subject to multiple risks, including geopolitical tensions, global commodity price volatility, unanticipated adjustments in energy tariffs, further uptick in wheat and allied product prices and adverse weather conditions,” it said.
The central bank had held the rate steady since raising it by 100 basis points in April in response to rising global energy prices and supply chain risks — its first increase in nearly three years.

stories.title: Fact-check: Viral video of Chinese freight train to Afghanistan is from Oct 2024
summary: However, the video is from October 2024 and shows the resumption of direct freight train services between China and Afghanistan.
The same video was also shared on the same day by another X user with the caption: “Afghanistan now has a railway connection to China with the help of Iranian engineering firms.

On October 25, a pro-Iran user on X, based on its past posts and profile picture, shared a video of a Chinese train with the following caption: “Afghanistan now has a railway connection to China with the help of Iranian engineering firms.

stories.title: LHC disposes of petition seeking release of Imran's sisters after govt extends detention
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday disposed of a petition seeking the release of PTI founder Imran Khan’s three sisters after the Punjab government informed the court that their preventive detention had been extended for another 30 days.

An assistant advocate general of Punjab told Justice Abher Gul Khan, who has been holding hearings on the petition, that the government had approved a further 30-day detention of Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi on the recommendation of the Lahore deputy commissioner.

Aleema’s son, Shahrez, had filed the petition alleging that the three sisters remained confined at Kot Lakhpat jail despite the end of their initial 30-day detention orders on Oct 19 for Aleema and 20 for Noreen and Uzma.

stories.title: Jordan arrests 3 in dawn raid over church attack
summary: Jordanian security forces on Monday arrested three suspects over an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, with the trio wounded in a dawn raid and shootout, authorities said.
Earlier, the king visited the injured victims of the church attack in hospital, dressed in military fatigues and carrying a pistol on his hip. “We will show them,” he vowed.

On Friday, Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning for the victims of the church attack, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public institutions.

stories.title: Pakistan, China call for enhanced cooperation between foreign ministries: FO
summary: During the third round of the Pakistan-China Spokespersons’ Dialogue in Islamabad on Monday, the two countries called for bolstered cooperation between their foreign ministries as well as in the areas of media engagement and strategic communication, the Foreign Office (FO) said.
Dar also stressed the importance of enhanced media cooperation, strategic communication and public diplomacy to advance bilateral relations and foster closer people-to-people ties.
Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and regional connectivity.

stories.title: Lahore ranks second globally as air pollution persists across Punjab
summary: Lahore ranked second among the world's most polluted major cities on IQAir's live air quality tracker on Monday, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 199, as pollution remained a concern across Punjab ahead of the peak winter smog season.
IQAir's Lahore city page recorded an AQI of 139 at 3pm on October 26, with fine particulate matter (PM2.5) identified as the main pollutant at 51 micrograms per cubic metre.
The reading placed Lahore in the unhealthy-for-sensitive-groups category on the US AQI scale.

stories.title: Faysal Quraishi, Hareem Farooq raise concerns over alleged paid campaign against 'Mango Jutt'
summary: Quraishi addressed the issue in an Instagram video, questioning the practice of publishing negative reviews without watching a film and warning that paid propaganda could undermine the industry’s efforts to bring audiences back to cinemas.
Meanwhile, Farooq, who produced and stars in the film, shared screenshots on Instagram that appeared to raise questions about whether some negative posts about the film had been paid for.
View this post on Instagram Screenshots shared in connection with the discussion included an exchange about whether a negative post concerning the film was paid content.

stories.title: After Vucic defeat, Serbia waits to learn how student-backed leaders will govern
summary: Tens of thousands took to the streets of Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia after Vucic conceded defeat late on Sunday, capping two years of peaceful anti-government protests calling for the populist ruler to step down.

With almost 99% of votes counted, the students' candidates had secured a commanding 52.7% of the vote, according to the State Election Commission, versus 39.2% for Vucic's Serbia Progressive Party (SNS)-led alliance.
Meanwhile, supporters of the student movement set about cleaning up a park near the parliament building in Belgrade that had long been used as a camp by Vucic's supporters.

stories.title: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations
summary: The Afghan Taliban have repeatedly claimed civilian casualties in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan; Pakistani authorities have denied the accusations, holding that they target military and terrorist infrastructure.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan.

It also rebutted the Afghan Taliban’s stance that it lacked the “capabilities” to fuel insecurity in other countries and criticised it for resorting to “diversionary allegations” instead of preventing the use of Afghanistan’s soil for terrorist attacks against Pakistan.

stories.title: Pakistan, US agree to enhance cooperation in energy sector
summary: Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik on Monday held a meeting with United States Chargé d’Affaires (Cd'A) Natalie Baker to discuss avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector.
During the meeting, Malik briefed Natalie on the measures taken by Pakistan to ensure energy security amid the evolving geopolitical situation.

On September 2, Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) signed a contract with Baker Hughes, a US energy technology company, to deploy Mature Assets Solutions aimed at revitalising ageing oil and gas wells and increasing Pakistan's indigenous hydrocarbon production.

stories.title: Dictionary.com names 'maxxing' its 2026 Word of the Year
summary: Dictionary.com said its selection was based on an analysis of search data, social media trends and news coverage, as well as the word's cultural significance.
The choice marks a contrast with Dictionary.com's 2025 Word of the Year, “67,” a viral expression whose meaning often remained unclear to users.
Other 2026 Finalists Dictionary.com selected finalists from internet culture, politics, technology and wider media trends.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks targeting Makkah, Madina as 'grave violation' of Saudi sovereignty
summary: Pakistan on Monday condemned Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s Makkah and Madina regions, terming them a “grave violation” of the kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Saudi Civil Defence said debris from intercepted missiles had fallen in the Makkah and Madina regions.
The Houthis subsequently denied targeting Makkah and Madina, saying their operations were directed at “Saudi oil facilities and military bases”.

stories.title: Netanyahu denies reports of clash with Israeli army chief over Iran-linked operation ahead of election
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday denied reports of a clash with Army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir over a proposed military operation that could trigger fighting with Iran ahead of Israel’s election.
Netanyahu denied any dispute with Zamir during an interview with Israel’s Channel 14 later on Sunday. “There is no confrontation,” he said.
We absolutely must send him home.” Netanyahu also claimed Iran had resumed its nuclear programme and portrayed the election as a matter of Israel’s survival.

stories.title: China's Xi opens Communist Party plenum, aims for firm governance measures
summary: China's Communist Party ​began a meeting of senior cadres on Monday aimed at tightening discipline and pressing officials to implement Beijing's orders, ‌paving the way for a leadership reshuffle next year expected to extend President Xi Jinping's rule for another five years.

Read: China's Communist Party ousts former ministers from Central Committee The Central Committee will convene in a closed-door meeting from Monday to Thursday, the fifth ​such gathering since the current cohort was formed in 2022 and therefore known as the "fifth plenum".

"It is likely ​everything will be centred on him, to dispel any rumours or doubts about his physical fitness and ability to continue in his role." China’s Communist Party is gathering for its most important meeting of the year: the fifth plenum.
